Class CausalStreams

java.lang.Object
io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.CausalStreams
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public final class CausalStreams extends Object implements AutoCloseable
A running Parsley application, created by Parsley.streams(Properties) and started here.

Exposes a restricted subset of KafkaStreams, with no accessor for the underlying instance. Where a member is absent, use the alternative:

  • Interactive queries and store(): observe state through sinks. The protocol store is internal, and under exactly-once semantics a local store holds the open transaction's writes until commit or abort, so a query can observe fold state that is not a function of any delivered history.
  • pause() and resume(): stop the instance, or scale by instances. Pausing one instance freezes its release punctuator and stalls every instance waiting on its outputs.
  • Thread add/remove and cleanUp(): scale by instances, and delete the state directory of a stopped instance.

    • setUncaughtExceptionHandler

      public void setUncaughtExceptionHandler(org.apache.kafka.streams.errors.StreamsUncaughtExceptionHandler handler)
      Registers the processing-exception handler. Call before start().

      The handler is registered totalized. One that throws, or returns null, resolves to SHUTDOWN_CLIENT, and the processing failure and the handler's own failure are both logged.

      Parameters:
      handler - the handler to consult for each uncaught processing exception

    • explainHolds

      public List<HeldRecord> explainHolds()
      Returns records currently held at the gate, longest-held first.

      One entry per gating head across this instance's local tasks, each naming the causes it still waits for and the local watermarks that show the gap.

      A held record means a cause is missing, lagging, or unstamped. Deliver the cause. Do not skip, reorder, or add a timeout. Each HeldRecord.Diagnosis names its case.

      Returns coordinates, claims, and watermarks, never key or value bytes. Reads a snapshot each task publishes from its own stream thread, refreshed on the wall-clock punctuator. A reading may be that stale, and describes an in-flight view that an aborted transaction may roll back.

      Returns:
      the held records, longest-held first, or an empty list when nothing is held
